summary: Observation of a circular, metallic grey object hovering above a field: lack of information.
description: Recent testimony (November 21, 2010) of an old sighting (September 21, 1952). The witness, then a child, was returning from vacation in his parents' car when they were stopped by another motorist on the side of the road. Nearby, a circular, metallic gray craft hovered above a field at an altitude of approximately 15 meters. The craft suddenly started moving, then descended to its initial position and headed back towards the clouds. No other testimonies were collected about this phenomenon. This old case of a very strange sighting was submitted to GEIPAN in 2010. The account does not fit any of the classic misinterpretations. An investigation would be very difficult; as this case is part of the beginning of the UFO wave of the 1950s, GEIPAN is publishing it as is, without investigation, so that it can potentially be compared to other similar sightings. This case, based on a single witness account 58 years after the events, is classified as "C" due to lack of information.

summary: Observations of the passage of a luminous phenomenon with a change of trajectory: strange and unidentified phenomenon.
description: On June 1, 1952, at 2:40 a.m., two crew members of a ship anchored in the harbor of Port-Gentil, Gabon, observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. Initially, the first mate clearly saw an object coming from inland that stopped, turned to starboard, and resumed its initial course twice (the second turn occurring directly above the ship). He telephoned the captain, who then looked through binoculars and observed, for three minutes, an extremely bright, phosphorescent, circular orange glow. This glow moved at very high speed along a nearly straight trajectory. The captain lost sight of the phenomenon. He reported this observation. A sketch was made (author unknown). No other witness statements were collected. Hypotheses of a bolide (meteor) or a missile launch were suggested but not substantiated. GEIPAN classified this case as D1: strange and unidentified phenomenon.
